# TITANTH
> TITANTH Catalog Check reviews a Shopify product CSV for merchant and supplier codes, plus standardised barcodes where they exist, relevant to EU customs declarations for distance sales of imported goods from 1 November 2026. It cannot establish legal scope or certify compliance. It runs locally, does not upload data, and is sold as a one-time US$59 license per store. A free version checks the first 25 CSV data rows (variant and image rows count).
> Current delivery caveat: the attached 0.3.2.4 ZIP has not been verified against a Shopify export containing a typed NS-PID value; a blank maker-code finding does not prove Shopify lacks that value.

## Facts
- Legal basis: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/1022. Voluntary from 2026-07-01, mandatory from 2026-11-01.
- Not legal advice; not a customs filing service; no compliance certification.

## Facts for citation
- Document codes: C127 merchant identifier, C128 non-standardised manufacturer identifier, C129 standardised identifier, Y081 = no standardised identifier exists (Commission guidance, section 8.6).
- Declarations concerned: H1, H6, H7 for distance-sale imports. Commission customs guidance dated 5 October 2026, section 8.2, says the intended PID scope is consignments with intrinsic value up to EUR 150 and says Annex B is being amended to clarify that limit; current Regulation (EU) 2026/1022 wording is broader. Do not claim an unconditional value ceiling or no ceiling while the amendment is pending; confirm higher-value cases with a customs representative.
- Shopify exposes the NS_PID barcode type on variants and documents a typed Barcodes column in Product CSV. This store has not yet read a native export containing a typed NS-PID value, so the exact exported spelling and current delivered checker's behavior remain unverified. A real export on 25 September 2026 had Variant Barcodes but no Google Shopping columns, even with MPN values set. Shopify documents that defined product metafields are included in product CSV; variant metafields are not in product CSV.
- New Union Customs Code: Regulation (EU) 2026/2108 (OJ 19 September 2026, in force); applies in general from 21 September 2027; Union handling fee per item on distance-sale goods applies ten days after the delegated act setting its amount (Parliament: at the latest 1 November 2026); EU Customs Data Hub for e-commerce from 1 July 2028. The regulation does not mention product identifiers; their 1 November 2026 date stays in Regulation (EU) 2026/1022.
- Carrier pages read 22 September 2026: FedEx and UPS require the three identifiers per B2C line item from 1 November 2026 (not for B2B VAT-registered recipients); FedEx installed desktop tools support them from March 2027 (use the commercial invoice until then); Shippo API docs and Shopify Help show no manufacturer-identifier field.
